The data thinning is controlled with these attributes:

Drawing lines for every sample when displaying a lot of data (such as a buffer~ containing a large audio sample) may put an unneccesary drain on computational resources. When displaying the contents of a buffer~, you can choose to  thin the data  so  that not all samples are not drawn
definerange -1 1, definepoint none, definethickness 1, refer drums

labels for specific points in the domain or range
The 'defineylabels' and 'definexlabels' messages take pairs of numbers and symbols.  The number specifies where to place the symbol.
coordinates in the plot at which to draw grid lines and lables are specified in terms of the domain and range you specify for the subplot.
grids and labels often only need to be defined for one of the subplots rather than for all of them.
the range (vertical dimension) is defined with a start point and an end point.
the domain (horizontal dimension) is defined with a start point, an end point, and an optional linear/log scale.
domains, ranges, and grids, are defined independently for each subplot, just as other appearance characteristics.
Your signal vector size must be 1/4 the FFT size or smaller for this patcher to work correctly!
To see only the frequencies from zero hertz up to the nyquist frequency, set the @audioframesize attribute to match the FFT frame size and set the @numpoints attribute to half the @audioframesize.
Use plot~ to graph high-resolution spectral responses from FFT.  Use multiple subplots to compare spectral responses.  In this example, the impact of windowing an FFT is made clear.
use plot~ to graph a live audio signal in order to see a visual represenation of the samples in that audio signal.
